sources.entry: Anki Miner - Desktop app for automated Anki language vocabulary card creation from video, audio, manga and books, in 32 languages.

summary.one_liner: Anki Miner is a desktop app that turns native-language video, audio, manga and book content into Anki vocabulary cards, supporting 32 languages.
summary.what_it_does: Anki Miner reads subtitles from a video/subtitle pair, batch folder, YouTube or Bilibili URL, or series, and splits the text into words. It filters those words to content words you do not already know, optionally letting you review candidates in a Word Curator. For each line it can grab a screenshot and audio clip, look up definitions in offline dictionaries (Yomitan format), and send finished cards to Anki through the AnkiConnect add-on. The Reading tab handles manga (mokuro), novels (.epub, .txt), subtitle files and pasted text, and the Audiobooks tab handles audiobooks, podcasts and songs. A Utilities tab offers local Whisper subtitle generation, subtitle retiming, yt-dlp downloads, deck copying and card backfill.
use_cases: create Anki flashcards from Japanese or Chinese anime and TV shows
make vocabulary cards from manga pages
mine words from epub novels into Anki
build a frequency-ranked deck from a video series
generate subtitles with local Whisper and make cards from them
backfill definitions and audio on existing Anki cards
how_to_run: Install Anki and the AnkiConnect add-on (code 2055492159)
Download the installer for your platform from the latest release, or run: pipx install anki-miner
Optional: pipx install "anki-miner[languages]" to add language engines
From source: git clone the repo, cd anki_miner, pip install -e ., then anki_miner_gui
notable: Supports 32 mining languages, with Japanese, Indonesian and Hebrew needing no extra engine download
Word Curator lets you review each candidate word with its scene, manga page and dictionary entry side by side
Undo a run by deleting the notes it just created from the results dialog
Embedded libmpv video preview for playing scenes while curating or adjusting subtitle timing
29 built-in colour themes and saveable settings profiles
caveats: Requires Anki running with the AnkiConnect add-on; video preview and pip/source installs need ffmpeg and libmpv
Unsigned builds trigger macOS, Windows SmartScreen and Linux AppImage first-run friction
Some features are limited on Intel macOS (no AVIF screenshots or silence removal for generated subtitles)
Dictionaries and frequency lists must be obtained separately; a fresh install has no definitions until resources are downloaded
